title: Past tenses: negatives and questions
intro: Read this before the questions on the past simple, past continuous and past perfect.

blocks.title: past simple
items: **Negative:** subject + **did not (didn't)** + base verb: She **didn't go**.
The past form moves into did, so the main verb returns to the base form: She went, but She **didn't go** (not *didn't went*) and **Did** she **go**? (not *Did she went?*).
**be** has no did: She **wasn't** late. **Was** she late? (not *Did she was late?*)

blocks.title: past continuous
items: **Negative:** subject + **was / were** + not + verb-ing: They **weren't playing**.
**Use:** an action in progress at a past moment: What **were** you **doing** at nine?

blocks.title: past perfect
items: **Negative:** subject + **had not (hadn't)** + past participle: He **hadn't left**.
**Past perfect continuous:** He **hadn't been working**. **Had** she **been waiting**? Only had moves; been and the -ing verb stay behind the subject.
**Use:** the EARLIER of two past actions: **Had** the film **started** when you arrived?

blocks.title: the two big traps
items: **did + past form** is wrong: *Did you saw it?* becomes **Did you see it?**
**did + had** is wrong for the past perfect: *Did she had left?* becomes **Had she left?** The helper is already had.
do / did is never added in the past continuous or in the perfect tenses.
